The three members' pass properties were extended to both cells to match.

If they are the same, the corpus has a redundant cell, which over-covers and costs a fixture; if they differ, both are needed and dropping either under-covers. Over-coverage is not a defect and under-coverage is, so the conservative choice is correct. It is also not the candidate's decision to make: narrowing two live formulations to one is an act for an authority that can amend a source.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with two advisories. Thirteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 6d066ef5 at 0444, 10485 bytes, unmoved and unedited; frozen v1 at 7ac3ddfd and my v1 verdict at e3dddee9, both agreeing with the dispatch and both stable; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26. Seven of seven cited digests reproduce. Both findings landed, and the blocker landed on its hard half. The corpus class now exists with its own exact-byte intent and pass property, where v1 had none. All three NT-3 strings are present and character-exact against preview-analyze-contract.v2's negativeTests — name, input and pass — with the source path named on the object. And the reconciliation I asked for is the part I expected to be fudged and is not: registerFormVerbatim carries the live claim character-exact beside v2's inputVerbatim, corpusTakesBothReadings is true, and readingNote states that the register's missing rung and v2's unconstructible universe are two cells of one NT-3 class rather than two NT numbers, that a fixture author must pin both, and that the specification does not collapse them. Two cells follow with the right ids and tags. That is the correct disposition of an ambiguity a candidate has no authority to settle: it cannot under-cover, it invents no NT number, and it leaves any narrowing to an act that can amend a source. I attacked the repair from both sides — collapse or invented number on one, dropping the register reading or over-extending the corpus on the other — and neither holds. The SHOULD-FIX landed the stronger of the two ways I offered: neither 'unknown-converted-to-covered' nor 'is not a sealed Run' survives in any member's retained bytes, and EV-1 and EV-3 each say so on the intent side and again on the pass side, so the two cannot drift apart later. The boundaries themselves are untouched and still correct. Nothing regressed: zero paths removed, EV-2 untouched since neither finding reached it, and the eleven changed values all sit inside the two findings' scope plus housekeeping. Two advisories carry, both partly addressed. failsIf now exists — v1 had none — but self-tests only the two folded findings rather than the standing attacks, and whatThisCloses, a global passProperty, a punctuation-discipline block and proposedLaterWork are still absent, so the artifact still names no obligation a recorder could attach to; the upside is that it coins no OBL- identifier and so avoids the gate-row-booking advisory now standing against G07, G18, G20 and G24. And of the six gate boundaries doesNot disclaims, G27 gained real treatment as a side effect of the SF1 repair, leaving G26, G28 and G30 asserted without being drawn. Neither is a reason to author a v3. This ACCEPT closes nothing by itself: the artifact claims no leftover closure and names no obligation.
